$comment: CANDIDATE. Options offered to the historian for each of the five R (needs-historian) anchors. Each option is a time on the anchor's own date, with the source basis read from docs/plan/data/time-facts.csv and the disagreement register (docs/plan/specialists/time-facts.md section 4). No option is a finding: every one is a reading of a source the specialist consulted, and the historian may supply a different time and range. Consequences (slopes, clocks, residuals, keyframe speeds) are computed by tools/time/build-review-packet.mjs, never typed here. 'default' marks the time currently proposed in time_anchors.json.

75.title: Lee's discretionary order to Ewell ("if practicable")
75.question: When did Lee's order (carried by Col. Taylor) reach Ewell, in local time? The site's chronology puts it at tick 75; the Turning Points page uses tick 175.

options.basis: start of the accepted range (R037 4:30-5:30 PM); no source states it
R037 best time; a search summary says Taylor sent the order "after 5 p.m."; Wikipedia first day gives no clock time
Stone Sentinels (SS1) places it in the block after Hancock's 5:25 PM dispatch to Meade (R036); disagreement register #10

read: Pfanz, Culp's Hill and Cemetery Hill (Ewell's decision)
OR 27/2 reports of Ewell, Early, Rodes and Johnson
75.note: Neighbours: t72 Hancock reaches Cemetery Hill 4:20 PM, t90 XII Corps arrives 6:00 PM. The order must fall after Lee reached the field (R024, 1:30-3:00 PM range) and is context for R038 (Johnson too late to attack).

90.title: XII Corps and Johnson's division arrive (R038 / R039)
90.question: When did the head of the XII Corps (Geary) and Johnson's Confederate division reach the field, in local time? The two fact rows are both ranges (4:30-7:00 PM and 5:00-8:00 PM); the proposal sits at 6:00 PM although both rows' own best time is 5:30 PM.

options.basis: both fact rows' own best time (R038, R039); Stone Sentinels (SS1) 5:30 PM Slocum approached
current proposal: keeps the slope to the nightfall design anchor (t100 8:00 PM) moderate
R038's range runs to 7:00 PM ("late afternoon"/"evening"); no clock time located

read: Pfanz, Culp's Hill and Cemetery Hill
OR 27/2 Ewell, Johnson; OR 27/1 Slocum, Geary, Williams
90.note: A search summary says Geary reached Gettysburg at 5 PM. Both rows are tagged S (search summary) or SS1; no primary report was read. The anchor is a compromise between two ranges, not a measurement.

248.title: Sickles advances III Corps to the Emmitsburg Road / Peach Orchard (R050)
248.question: When did Sickles's advance begin? The accepted range is noon to 3:30 PM; the proposal is the midpoint, 2:30 PM. The site's vignette V-007 says "around 3:00".

options.basis: Wikipedia second day "after noon he became concerned"; Stone Sentinels (SS2) "Noon"; kept 30 minutes after the t240 Berdan probe (12:00)
current proposal: midpoint of the accepted range (R050 best)
the site's own vignette V-007 ("around 3:00"): an authored claim, not a source; Meade's 3 PM corps commanders' meeting is R051

read: OR 27/1 Sickles, Birney, Warren, Sykes; Meade's testimony
248.note: Register #11: Hessler and Pfanz differ; the specialist marked it needs-historian. The clock between t240 (12:00) and t256 (4:00 PM) runs at 18.8 and 11.2 min/tick around this anchor.

275.title: Chamberlain's 20th Maine bayonet charge (R066)
275.question: When did the 20th Maine charge downhill? Sources span 5:10 PM to after 7 PM. Register #17 is the strongest disagreement and says: do not present a minute-precise time. This is the hero moment of the site's tour, Turning Points and onboarding.

options.basis: a participant timeline via a search summary (SRCH)
Stone Sentinels (SS2) and The History Junkie (THJ) 5:30 PM block
current proposal: "a defensible mid value, labelled approximate" (the fact row's own best is 6:15 PM)
Desjardin-derived summary "by 6:30 ... fix bayonets" (SRCH, HNc). Collides with the t280 Peach Orchard anchor (6:30 PM)
Cross via HistoryNet: "after 7 p.m.". Later than the t280 and t295 anchors

read: Desjardin, Stand Firm Ye Boys from Maine
Oates's account and OR 27/2 (Longstreet, McLaws, Law, Oates)
275.note: Options D and E place the charge after the Peach Orchard collapse (t280) that the specialist anchors at 6:30 PM: choosing them means re-timing t280 and t295 too, which is a larger decision. The 15th Alabama's first assault (R060) is 4:30-5:00 PM per timelines but 6 PM per one HistoryNet reading (outlier).

538.title: Pickett-Pettigrew-Trimble infantry step off (R108)
538.question: When did the infantry step off from Seminary Ridge? The accepted range is 2:00-3:00 PM; the proposal is 3:00 PM. Wikipedia's own two articles disagree (about 2:00 vs around 3:00). This anchor sits under the site's 20-second hero moment (ticks 535-556), so it is the first item to review.

options.basis: Wikipedia Pickett's Charge "about 2:00 p.m." (citing Coddington p.502, Hess p.162, Sears p.415, Wert p.182); Longstreet OR "About 2 p.m. Pickett reported ... in order" (a report about the line, not the step-off)

Stone Sentinels (SS3) 2:30-3:00; the specialist's consistency check: a 2:00 step-off would put the lines at the wall by about 2:30, contradicting the 3:10-3:45 arrival every source read gives, so the step-off cannot be much earlier than about 2:30-2:45

current proposal: American Battlefield Trust ("stepped off in unison at about 3:00 p.m.") and Wikipedia's main article ("Around 3 p.m.", citing Coddington p.402, McPherson p.662, Eicher p.546, Trudeau p.484, Walsh p.281)

read: Hessler and Motts, Pickett's Charge at Gettysburg
Alexander, Fighting for the Confederacy; OR 27/2 Longstreet, Alexander, Pendleton
538.note: The neighbours t518 (cannonade opens 1:07 PM, sourced H) and t551 (Armistead over the wall 3:35 PM) bound the choice: an earlier step-off stretches the ticks between the step-off and the wall. Cushing, Armistead and Hancock monument tooltips say 3:00, 3:15 and 3:20 PM (15-35 minutes early against the sources).

design_and_circular.226: Day-2 start design anchor: first light 4:30 AM (civil dawn 4:03, sunrise 4:35). Owner signs.
design_and_circular.675: Nominal end of battle design anchor: 8:00 PM July 3 (sunset 7:32, twilight ends 8:04). Owner signs.
